title: Finite cohomology windows control bounded-below derived sections
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ be a strictly full subcategory containing zero and closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between its objects and under extensions. Fix $U\in\mathcal C$ and an integer $d\geq0$ such that $H^p(U,M)=0$ for every $M\in\mathcal S$ and every $p>d$. Here $R\Gamma(U,-)$ is the right derived functor of sections, followed by forgetting scalars, and $H^r(U,E)=H^r(R\Gamma(U,E))$; a sheaf is placed in degree zero. Let $f:E\to F$ be a morphism in $D(\mathcal O)$, where $E,F$ are bounded below (each has zero cohomology below some integer, with no common bound prescribed) and all their cohomology sheaves belong to $\mathcal S$. For integers $a\leq b$, suppose that $H^q(f)$ is an isomorphism whenever $a-d-1\leq q\leq b+1$. Then the actual induced map
$$H^r(U,f):H^r(U,E)\longrightarrow H^r(U,F)$$
is an isomorphism for every $a\leq r\leq b$. No covering-basis, exact-product, or uniform lower-bound hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D6T, label lemma-olsson-laszlo-modified, proof, first paragraph: finite-window comparison of the bounded-below hypercohomology spectral sequences; formulated for an individual morphism and a single site object.

proof.text: Put $v=\Gamma(U,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\operatorname{Ab}$, forgetting the section-ring action. It is additive and left exact: addition is sectionwise and a kernel of module sheaves is computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The source category is Grothendieck and admits K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The target is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian] with $R=\mathbf Z$ (abelian groups are precisely $\mathbf Z$-modules). Thus the derived functor $Rv$ in the hypercohomology theorem is the specified $R\Gamma(U,-)$, and its value on $M[0]$ computes the stated $H^p(U,M)$ by [lem-sp-kinjective-computes].

source.place: Tag 07A5, section-unbounded, construction of derived evaluation; derived.tex Tag 015J, lemma-two-ss-complex-functor

proof.text: Complete $f$ to a distinguished triangle $E\xrightarrow f F\to C\to E[1]$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives $0\to\operatorname{coker}H^q(f)\to H^q(C)\to\ker H^{q+1}(f)\to0$. Since the two outer objects lie in $\mathcal S$, so does $H^q(C)$, by exactly the kernel, cokernel and extension hypotheses. If $E,F$ vanish below $m$, then this sequence gives $H^q(C)=0$ for $q<m-1$; choose $m$ to be the minimum of their two lower bounds. Further, the assumed isomorphisms give $H^q(C)=0$ for $a-d-1\le q\le b$, since both $q$ and $q+1$ are in the assumed interval.

source.place: Tag 05RS, lemma-cohomology-homological; Tag 05RU, derived category and cone triangles

proof.text: The standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] supplies a bounded-below complex representing $C$, because its cohomology is bounded below by Step 2. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to this complex and the functor $v$ of Step 1. It gives a convergent spectral sequence with $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(U,H^q(C))$, zero for $p<0$, and finite exhaustive separated filtrations of $H^t(U,C)$ whose graded pieces are $E_\infty^{p,t-p}$. Its use with the specified K-injective derived sections is legitimate by [lem-sp-kinjective-computes]: a bounded-below injective resolution computes the same derived functor. All cohomology sheaves $H^q(C)$ belong to $\mathcal S$, so the bound in the hypothesis also gives $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $p>d$.

source.place: Tag 015J, lemma-two-ss-complex-functor; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6T, lemma-olsson-laszlo-modified, first paragraph

proof.text: Fix $a\le r\le b$ and take $t=r-1$ or $t=r$. On total degree $t$, terms with $p<0$ or $p>d$ vanish by Step 3. For $0\le p\le d$, the index $q=t-p$ satisfies $a-d-1\le q\le b$, so Step 2 makes $H^q(C)=0$ and hence $E_2^{p,q}=0$. A zero term stays zero on each later page, since each next term is the kernel of the outgoing differential modulo the image of the incoming differential. Therefore every $E_\infty$ term on this diagonal is zero. By the finite filtration and graded-piece assertion of [thm-sp-truncation-e2], every successive quotient of the filtration of $H^t(U,C)$ is zero. Starting at its zero endpoint and inducting through its finitely many steps gives $H^t(U,C)=0$. In particular $H^{r-1}(U,C)=H^r(U,C)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0D6T, lemma-olsson-laszlo-modified, first paragraph; diagonal vanishing calculation using derived.tex Tag 015J

proof.text: The right derived functor $Rv=R\Gamma(U,-)$ carries the triangle of Step 2 to a distinguished triangle, by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]; the K-injective hypotheses hold by Step 1 (and for the target by the Grothendieck resolution theorem [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence]). Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. The resulting exact segment is $H^{r-1}(U,C)\to H^r(U,E)\xrightarrow{H^r(U,f)}H^r(U,F)\to H^r(U,C)$. The outer groups vanish by Step 4, proving that the middle arrow is an isomorphism. It is the actual arrow $H^r(R\Gamma(U,f))$ because the triangle is obtained by applying that functor to the original triangle; no comparison map was chosen anew.
